questions.q: Basis has one identity rule it really wants you to remember. Basis is a ___, not a platform.
a: Social VR app with extra steps
questions.fact: Straight from the philosophy page: 'Basis is a framework, not a platform.' You can build a platform WITH it; Basis itself doesn't run one.

questions.q: What's BasisVR's actual tagline?
questions.fact: It's the title of every page on basisvr.org. 'Jiggle Responsibly' is still available for merch.

questions.q: Basis is open source under which license?
questions.fact: Every page ends with 'BasisVR. MIT Licensed.' Do (almost) whatever you want with it.

questions.q: Basis is built with which engine-and-language combo?
questions.fact: The philosophy page calls it 'a set of Unity/C# libraries and a demo showing how components fit together.' No spreadsheets were harmed.

questions.q: Which Unity render pipeline is Basis built on?
a: Whichever one the avatar's shader demands
questions.fact: 'Built with URP, targeting IL2CPP.' Please stop importing HDRP shaders.

questions.q: Basis targets which scripting backend? (Yes, the one that makes builds take forever.)
a: A guy named Steve who types very fast
questions.fact: IL2CPP turns .NET IL into C++ and compiles it to native code ahead of time. Steve is not real. Yet.

questions.q: Basis names three building blocks of good VR: Presence, Spatialization, and ___.
questions.fact: Embodiment: 'a tight, continuous loop between your body and its representation.' Snacks are still recommended.

questions.q: Per community feedback quoted on the site, why do people wrongly assume Basis is a platform?
questions.fact: The quote: 'People think Basis is a platform because tests run on servers. Keep a hard focus on it being a framework.'

questions.q: Which of these is NOT on the homepage's list of basics Basis handles for you?
questions.fact: The real list: XR input, audio, player controller, networking, asset bundle loading, 'and more.' Emotional support is handled by the Discord, unofficially.

questions.q: According to the philosophy page, who works on Basis full-time?
a: Three raccoons in a trench coat
An intern who was never told they could leave
The jiggle system, which became self-aware
questions.fact: Donations 'directly support their livelihood and the project's momentum.' The raccoons are volunteers.

questions.q: Basis is operated by a group of trusted contributors. What are they called?
questions.fact: The Pillars keep the effort 'on the narrow straight' so the project stays aligned and doesn't get derailed.

questions.q: Where does Basis collect community donations?
questions.fact: Donations plus companies funding shared infrastructure keep the lights on. The jar is a rumour.

questions.q: The site names two hard problems solved by pooling funds from multiple organizations. Which pair?
a: The jiggle system and QUIC integration
Fixing that one bug and the other one
questions.fact: Bundling funds from several orgs lets Basis tackle problems that benefit everyone. Yes, physics bounce was one of them.

questions.q: How often do the Talk & Test sessions happen?
questions.fact: 'Join us weekly for our Talk & Test sessions - connect, create, and stress-test VR together.' The server's feelings are not tracked.

questions.q: Basis would rather you use its own XR system than which Unity toolkit?
questions.fact: Basis says its XR system is 'built with real, hard-won experience from testing against a wide range of hardware.' Mixing in other stacks is a roadmap goal.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four numbered principles on the philosophy page?
a: Ship It Friday, Fix It Monday
questions.fact: The real four: Creator-First, Creative Freedom by Design, Communication is Expression, and Framework, Not Platform.

questions.q: The planned neutral demo scene for museums, dataviz, theater and 'serious' apps is called the ___.
questions.fact: Showroom: spawning props, sync'd interactions, avatar basics, conservative defaults. The example props are literally 'car, robots.'

questions.q: Basis plans a second, experimental client for strain-testing features that 'may change rapidly'. Its name?
questions.fact: The Community Testbed is the successor to today's ad-hoc tests and explicitly NOT the public-facing showcase, so expect things to be on fire.

questions.q: The in-development quickstart doc promises clone, open project, press Play. What's it called?
questions.fact: Five minutes is the goal. Unity's first import is not included. Nothing can help you there.

questions.q: Basis isn't publicly on Steam yet. How does the site say you get in?
a: Buy it on the Steam store
Chant 'framework, not platform' into a mirror
Beat Dooly in a load test
Request a key from the admin team in Discord
questions.fact: Once approved, Discord also offers onboarding, support, and avatar porting help for Unity-based assets.

questions.q: The roadmap wants Basis modules shipped as what, so you can grab just networking without the whole stack?
questions.fact: Modularity is 'a roadmap goal, not fully realized yet.' final_FINAL_v2.zip remains the industry standard.

questions.q: The site describes Basis as 'whitelabel' and ___.
questions.fact: Fully rebrandable into your own VR space, and 'player assets remain compatible across instances.' Haunting not guaranteed.

questions.q: Which social network does the homepage list for 'Updates and Community posts'?
questions.fact: Twitter/X is listed separately for 'Short news & Release notes.' MySpace remains unclaimed.

questions.q: Finish the philosophy page's closing pitch: 'Use the framework. Keep your freedom. ___'
questions.fact: That's the 'Build with Basis' send-off. 'Blame the network' is the unofficial motto of every load test.
